Why August is running behind July

Commentary refreshed as at 11-Aug-2026 (11 days). Calendar mix: Aug 1-11 contains 4 weekend days against 3 in Jul 1-11 — but the mix now explains less of the gap than it did at the 10-day read: the ex-Sunday shortfall has widened from −3.6% to −6.5% after a soft Tuesday 11-Aug (₹1.25 Cr, the weakest weekday of the month so far).

1 · It is still volume, not price

Realization is broadly holding (both per-unit measures within −3%). The gap comes from fewer visits, fewer surgeries and a lighter census.

Surgeries remain the steepest volume decline (−16%). Occupancy is 6.8 points lighter on a slightly shorter ALOS — the census never rebuilt after the July month-end discharge run.

2 · The gap is concentrated, not broad-based

Declines total ₹24.9 L/day, offset by ₹6.6 L/day of gains, for a net ₹18.3 L/day. Nephrology and Medical Oncology alone are ₹9.4 L/day — 52% of the net gap.

4 · The read

The gap is widening, and it is now less about the calendar. At the 10-day read roughly half the headline shortfall was weekend mix; after Tuesday 11-Aug came in at ₹1.25 Cr the ex-Sunday gap has doubled to −6.5%, and the full-month projection has slipped to ₹41.2 Cr (−₹9.9 Cr vs budget). Weekday throughput itself is now soft.

The concentration is unchanged: Nephrology remains the deepest drag (Dr. Abi Abraham −40%, −₹4.2 L/day — dialysis revenue tracks scheduled slots filled) with Medical Oncology steady at −21% on Dr. Gangadharan's book. Cardiology has held its recovery (dept −4%) as Dr. Anandkumar offsets Dr. Cibi Issac. The neuro cluster keeps compounding (+₹6.6 L/day gross) but its offset is not growing as fast as the decliners are deepening. Watch items: GI Surgery (−35%), Ortho — Dr. Rajesh Simon (−64%), and Gastroenterology ex-Mukkada.

What to test first: dialysis session counts and slot utilisation for 01-11 August vs July; chemotherapy day-care volumes; OT list utilisation (surgeries/day −16% is the steepest operational decline); consultant availability for Nephrology, Medical Oncology, GI Surgery and Orthopedics; and whether the 10% OP funnel decline is walk-in or referral-led.

Caveat: Onam falls later in August and typically lifts elective volumes in the back half — the ₹41.2 Cr projection assumes the current run-rate holds and should be re-read after 15 August. If the back-half lift does not materialise, August lands roughly ₹8-10 Cr short of plan.
